claim: Detrimental semantic collapse -- where repeated samples for an underspecified prompt converge on a single confidently-wrong interpretation -- affects a non-trivial share of tasks even on benchmarks assumed well-specified.
stance_target: reliability of sampling-based (self-consistency/semantic-entropy) correctness prediction for code
scope_conditions: MBPP, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench v6, 3 SOTA coding models, Python
quoted_support: detrimental semantic collapse is prevalent even on benchmarks widely regarded as well-specified, affecting over 3% of HumanEval, 11% of MBPP, and 32% of LiveCodeBench tasks.

claim: Deliberately injecting underspecification into benchmark prompts increases detrimental collapse rates by up to 5.5x, and Pass@k gaps of up to 66.8% persist even at high sampling budgets (up to Pass@25) on MBPP.
stance_target: limits of repeated sampling as a fix for underspecification-driven miscalibration
quoted_support: we observe a significant gap in Pass@k of up to 66.8% compared to the original benchmark. For MBPP, this gap persists at higher sampling budgets (e.g. up to Pass@25), suggesting that repeated sampling alone is insufficient for LLMs to reliably produce the correct interpretation of underspecified tasks.
numbers: up to 5.5x increase in collapse rate

claim: Clustering-based semantic-entropy-style uncertainty methods fail silently under detrimental collapse because the incorrect implementation is produced consistently across generations, so entropy/disagreement reads as confident even though the model is wrong.
stance_target: robustness of internal sampling-consistency signals (e.g. semantic entropy, functional entropy) as a universal correctness proxy for code
scope_conditions: code generation with underspecified or ambiguous prompts
quoted_support: Under detrimental semantic collapse, clustering-based approaches fail silently, failures evade detection, as the incorrect implementation is consistent across generations, leaving users unaware of the underlying misalignment.

claim: The paper is a diagnostic study of a sampling-based-UQ failure mode; it does not evaluate verbalized confidence, ECE, AUROC, or any calibration training method.
quoted_support: competitive programming tasks have inherently low pass rate, yet LLMs still confidently produce semantically indistinguishable programs, frequently converging on an incorrect interpretation with no indication of uncertainty.
